A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ScienceBoard research work. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and reformatted content.

before.justification: v2 reports original agent and human success rates in Table 3, planner-grounding experiments in Table 4, and interface, stability, and difficulty analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations of additional backbones and compute-scaling experiments in Tables 9–10.

M1.justification: The ScienceBoard environment, unified action space, evaluation framework, and planner-grounding procedure are retained. Native reasoning modes are additional evaluation configurations; the PDFs do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 169 tasks across six scientific domains and retain the existing interface and interactive theorem-proving scenarios. The compute study uses three existing domains without introducing new task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 substantially expands the evaluated lineup: GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro enter screenshot and screenshot+a11ytree comparisons; GPT-oss-120B enters a11ytree; Qwen3-VL-235B and Kimi-2.5 enter screenshot comparisons. Earlier comparators, including the Table 4 grounding models, remain.

E3.justification: Appendix F.4 adds a screenshot evaluation with max_tokens of 1500, 2000, and 2500, plus GPT-5 medium/high reasoning-effort comparisons under two observation settings. The previously stated main-experiment temperature, top_p, and 1500-token limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F.4 adds focused sensitivity analyses asking whether larger generation budgets and native reasoning effort alleviate performance bottlenecks. Existing interface ablations, stability checks, difficulty analyses, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three independent GPT-4o stability runs and Figure 7 error bars, along with randomly sampled t-SNE seeds. The added results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical test.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds substantial results, including GPT-5's 24.20% overall success with screenshot+a11ytree; Tables 9–10 add budget- and reasoning-effort outcomes. Retained screenshot Overall scores also change: InternVL3-78B moves from 2.69% to 5.46%, while UI-TARS-1.5-7B moves from 5.46% to 2.69%, despite unchanged domain scores, indicating an apparent transposition.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, trajectory-probability equation (1), and mathematical task examples are retained. No new theoretical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract updates its example backbones and headline overall success figure from 15% to 20%. The environment and benchmark contributions and below-human-proficiency conclusion remain. The introduction still repeats the earlier 0–15% range.

C2.justification: Sections 5.2 and F.4 add the interpretation that additional reasoning provides bounded benefits while perception and action remain bottlenecks. The discussion further explains scientific knowledge and interface-selection requirements. The earlier binary-success and partial-credit limitations are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix C extends the existing access documentation with native Ubuntu deployment, Docker availability and repository information, and promised cloud guidelines. Existing hardware, preprocessing, and prompt details remain. The new compute configurations are reported, although Table 9 does not identify its backbone.

R1.justification: v3 adds Sänger et al. on scientific workflow development and references for GPT-5, Gemini-2.5, and gpt-oss. The central research positioning and Table 7 benchmark comparison remain. The retitled Lean Copilot reference identifies the same earlier cited work.

P1.justification: Selected paragraphs are shortened or rewritten, Section 6's analyses are reordered, and the discussion moves from main-text Section 7 to Appendix A. Ethics material is relocated, and acknowledgements and an LLM-writing disclosure are added. Most technical prose and all prompt content remain.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands, Tables 9–10 are added, and several displays are resized or relocated, including Figure 5 and Table 4. Conference formatting changes the title, headers, typography, and page layout. Existing Figures 1–13 retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: The expanded backbone evaluation and focused compute studies provide useful additional evidence about the benchmark's difficulty, while Appendix C improves access documentation. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by the apparent Table 3 score transposition, the stale introductory performance range, and Table 9's unspecified backbone, which weaken reporting consistency and interpretability.
